text:
Oh sea, enormous sea, fierce heart
of uneven rhythm, wicked heart,
I am softer than that poor stick
rotting, imprisoned in your waves.


Oh sea, give me your tremendous wrath,
I spent my life forgiving,
because I understood, sea, I gave myself away:
“Pity, pity for the one who most offends.”


Vulgarity, vulgarity hounds me.
Ah, the city and man have bought me.
Make me possess your nameless wrath:
this mission of a rose tires me now.


Do you see that vulgar man? He grieves me,
I lack air, and where it fails, I remain;
I wish I did not understand, but I cannot:
it is the vulgarity that poisons me.


I grew poorer because understanding overwhelms,
I grew poorer because understanding suffocates,
blessed be the strength of the rock!
I have a heart like foam.


Sea, I dreamed of being as you are,
there in the afternoons when my life
opened beneath the warm hours...
Ah, I dreamed of being as you are.


Look at me here, small, wretched,
every pain overcomes me, every dream;
sea, give me, give me the ineffable resolve
to become proud, unreachable.


Give me your salt, your iodine, your fierceness,
Sea air!... Oh storm, oh anger!
Unhappy me, I am a thistle,
and I die, sea, I succumb in my poverty.


And my soul is like the sea, it is that;
ah, the city rots and confounds it,
this petty life that provokes pain,
if only I could free myself from its weight!


Let my endeavor fly, let my hope fly...
My life should have been horrible,
it should have been an uncontainable artery,
and it is barely a scar that always aches.

translation.title: Facing the Sea
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sea’s direct address, the repeated “vulgarity,” and the contrast between oceanic force and the speaker’s diminished life.
